newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's two futures clearing houses to merge.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's two futures clearing houses to merge.

text.p: Malaysia's two clearing houses will on Monday sign an agreement to merge and establish a single clearing house for the trading of futures contracts, said a statement by one of the houses on Friday.
Malaysian Derivatives Clearing House Bhd said in a statement that the memorandum of understanding will be signed with Malaysian Futures Clearing Corp Sdn Bhd.

Other signatories will be the Malaysian futures bourses, the Kuala Lumpur Options & Financial Futures Exchange Bhd (KLOFFE), the Malaysia Monetary Exchange Bhd (MME) and the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange Bhd (KLCE).

"(The signing) sets out the commitment of the parties to the establishment of a single clearing house to provide clearing house facilities for all futures contracts traded on futures markets operated by KLOFFE, MME and KLCE," the statement said.
KLOFFE currently offers a futures contract based on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's key Composite Index.
The MME trades a futures contract based on the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered rate.
The KLCE offers futures contracts in palmoil, rubber, tin, cocoa and palm kernel oil.
The government has recently made calls for a single clearing house to be created for higher efficiency and reducing duplication.
